family_history: Father had hypertension and a stroke at 70

social_history.driving: Driving; his wife reports two near-misses at junctions

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and fully oriented. MoCA 26/30, which is within the normal range: he loses 1 point on trail-making, 1 on the cube, and 2 on delayed recall (3/5 unaided, 5/5 with cueing). Verbal fluency 16 animals. On direct questioning he cannot describe the sequence of a routine tax filing he has done for thirty years.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Pupils equal and reactive. Extraocular movements full. Visual fields full. Face symmetric. Speech normal.
neurological_exam.motor: Normal bulk. Tone mildly increased in both legs. Strength 5/5 throughout.
neurological_exam.sensory: Vibration mildly reduced at the toes.
neurological_exam.gait: Mildly short-stepped with a slightly widened base; arm swing preserved. Tandem possible for four steps. No falls.
neurological_exam.additional: Palmomental reflex present bilaterally. No parkinsonian features. Pulse regular at 74.

patient.chief_complaint: A normal cognitive screen in a professional who has lost the ability to do his job
patient.history_present_illness: Mr. Emanuele Costa is a 63-year-old senior tax consultant referred after his general practitioner recorded a MoCA of 26/30 and reassured him. His wife and his business partner disagree with that reassurance, and the partner has written a letter. Over two years he has become unable to carry a case: he cannot hold the structure of a filing in mind, has missed three statutory deadlines with financial consequences, produced two returns with errors a trainee would not make, and now has a colleague covering all of his work while he remains nominally employed. At home he can no longer plan a journey with a connection, has stopped doing the family accounts, and has twice put diesel in a petrol car. His wife reports two near-misses at junctions. He himself minimises all of it and attributes the errors to a heavy workload. His memory for events is good and improves with prompting. He had a lacunar stroke four years ago with full recovery, and has hypertension, diabetes and hyperlipidaemia, all imperfectly controlled with a blood pressure of 148/88 today. There are no hallucinations, no fluctuation, no dream enactment and no gait complaint.

findings.type: White matter hyperintensity of presumed vascular origin
findings.location: Confluent periventricular and deep white matter, frontal predominant

signal_characteristics.T2_FLAIR: Extensive confluent hyperintensity with frontal predominance and external capsule involvement

findings.location: Left thalamus, right corona radiata, left putamen, right internal capsule, left pons

signal_characteristics.SWI: Deep distribution; no lobar microbleed and no cortical superficial siderosis

findings.location: Mild global; medial temporal lobes normal for age

volumetrics.frontal_lesion_predominance: Marked — the anatomical correlate of the dysexecutive syndrome

additional_observations: Fazekas 3 confluent frontal-predominant white matter change with five lacunes, two of them strategically placed in the left thalamus and right internal capsule
The frontal predominance and the strategic lacune locations are the anatomical explanation for a severe dysexecutive syndrome with a preserved screening score
SWI shows two deep microbleeds and no lobar lesion or siderosis — hypertensive arteriopathy
Medial temporal lobes and hippocampi are normal for age, against a degenerative amnestic process
mri.impression: Severe frontal-predominant small-vessel disease: Fazekas 3 confluent white matter change, five lacunes including strategically placed thalamic and capsular lesions, and two deep microbleeds. The lesion distribution matches a dysexecutive syndrome and explains why a brief screen was insensitive to it.

labs.interpretation: HbA1c 7.9% and LDL 108 mg/dL are both above target for a patient with a prior stroke. TSH, B12, folate, RPR and HIV are normal or negative, excluding reversible causes.

findings.test: Behavioural Assessment of the Dysexecutive Syndrome — Zoo Map (planning)

quantitative_data.dissociation: planning and real-world task performance at the 1st percentile against naming at the 70th
quantitative_data.discrepancy_from_premorbid: greater than 3 standard deviations on executive measures

specialized_test.impression: The formal battery resolves what the screen concealed. Against an estimated premorbid IQ of 128, planning and real-world multitasking are at the 1st percentile with six rule breaks on the Multiple Errands Test, and only two of six Wisconsin categories were completed, while naming and recognition memory remain at or above the population average. The discrepancy from premorbid ability exceeds three standard deviations on executive measures. This is a severe dysexecutive syndrome that a brief screening instrument cannot detect in a highly educated patient.

scores.procedural_account: unable to describe the sequence of a task he has performed for 30 years

findings.performance: Only 1 point lost on the screen, but unable to describe a 30-year routine task sequence — severely impaired on functional probing
Digit span normal on the screen; fails when the task carries real content

clinical_assessment.impression: MoCA 26/30 is within the normal range and, in a man with two law and economics degrees and a career in tax, it is a substantial fall that the instrument cannot register — a ceiling effect in a high-baseline patient. The informant-rated functional scale is 23/30, occupational function is lost, insight is reduced, and he cannot describe the sequence of a task he performed for thirty years. The functional evidence, not the screen, establishes the diagnosis.

vascular_cognitive_impairment.query: vascular cognitive impairment diagnostic criteria and secondary prevention

results.title: Diagnostic criteria for vascular cognitive disorders: a VASCOG statement
results.authors: Sachdev P, Kalaria R, O'Brien J, et al.
results.summary: Requires a cognitive syndrome documented on a validated instrument plus imaging or temporal evidence that cerebrovascular disease accounts for it.

results.title: Neuroimaging standards for research into small vessel disease (STRIVE-2)
results.authors: Duering M, Biessels GJ, Brodtmann A, et al.
results.summary: Defines and standardises the reporting of white matter hyperintensity, lacunes, microbleeds, perivascular spaces and cortical superficial siderosis.

vascular_cognitive_impairment.summary: No disease-modifying therapy exists for vascular cognitive impairment; management is control of the vascular risk factors, secondary prevention matched to the mechanism, review of the anticholinergic burden, and treatment of coexisting Alzheimer pathology where biomarkers support it.

medication_review.proposed: review of the current medication list for anticholinergic burden
warnings: Anticholinergic load is a reversible contributor to cognitive impairment in this population and should be quantified before any new prescription.
medication_review.summary: No prohibitive interaction identified within the current list.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Vascular dementia — subcortical ischaemic (small-vessel) type with a severe dysexecutive syndrome, concealed by a normal screening score in a high-baseline patient

differential.key_features: The screening score and the patient's own account support it, and it is what the referral concluded — but occupational function is lost, the informant functional scale is 23/30, and formal executive testing is at the 1st percentile against a premorbid IQ of 128

differential.diagnosis: Occupational burnout or stress-related cognitive complaint
differential.key_features: The Geriatric Depression Scale is 3/15, the deficits are objective on formal testing, and there is a Fazekas 3 imaging burden with five lacunes
Recall is cue-responsive, recognition memory is above average, and the hippocampi are normal for age
Reduced insight is present, but there is no disinhibition, no loss of empathy, no compulsivity, no dietary change and no frontotemporal atrophy; the frontal syndrome here is subcortical and vascular
Not reported, no snoring or daytime somnolence volunteered, and the profile is not attentional

optimal_actions.action: Obtain a collateral history from an informant who sees the patient daily: the shape of the decline (abrupt, stepwise or gradual), whether any step can be dated to a cerebrovascular event, and which instrumental activities have been lost
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Two years of catastrophic occupational and instrumental failure documented by an employer and a spouse, in a man with a screening score in the normal range who minimises the problem himself

optimal_actions.action: Perform a validated bedside cognitive assessment and record the per-domain profile and whether delayed recall improves with cueing
optimal_actions.expected_finding: MoCA 26/30 within the normal range but a ceiling effect in a highly educated professional: informant functional scale 23/30, occupational function lost, insight reduced, and inability to describe a 30-year routine task

optimal_actions.action: Order the reversible-cause screen and the vascular-risk assays that will be treated (CBC, CMP, TSH, B12, folate, RPR, HIV, HbA1c, lipid panel)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Reversible causes excluded; HbA1c 7.9% and LDL 108 mg/dL above target after a lacunar stroke

optimal_actions.action: Perform timed gait and balance testing: the short-stepped, wide-based gait with preserved arm swing is part of the subcortical syndrome and separates it from the gait of normal pressure hydrocephalus and of parkinsonian disorders
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Timed-up-and-go 13.9 s with a markedly abnormal 34% dual-task decrement — objective evidence of executive failure in a patient whose screening score was normal

optimal_actions.action: Obtain brain MRI reported in STRIVE-2 terms — FLAIR for white matter hyperintensity with a Fazekas grade, T1/T2 for lacunes, DWI to establish that the lesions are chronic, and SWI for microbleeds and cortical superficial siderosis — together with the medial temporal atrophy grade
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Fazekas 3 frontal-predominant confluent change with five lacunes including strategic thalamic and capsular lesions and two deep microbleeds, with normal hippocampi

optimal_actions.action: Order formal multi-domain neuropsychological testing to settle the executive-versus-amnestic attribution and to document a baseline for follow-up
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Severe executive impairment on ecologically valid and demanding tests, against normal performance on brief bedside items — the dissociation that resolves the case

optimal_actions.action: Confirm the diagnostic criteria applied and the current secondary-prevention targets against the guidelines
optimal_actions.expected_finding: VASCOG 2014 criteria and the 2021 AHA/ASA secondary prevention targets confirmed

optimal_actions.action: Review the medication list for anticholinergic burden and for the interaction between antithrombotic choice and the microbleed burden before prescribing
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Anticholinergic contributors identified and the antithrombotic choice reconciled with the imaging burden

optimal_actions.action: Reverse the reassurance: state that the diagnostic threshold for dementia is functional, not a screening cut-off, and that it is met; notify the driving authority given two near-misses and a documented dysexecutive syndrome; arrange occupational health review and medical retirement planning at 63 with financial and legal safeguards, since he retains professional responsibility for other people's tax affairs; intensify blood pressure, glycaemic and lipid control as the only measures that slow progression; and arrange carer education with insight-adapted communication
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Diagnosis established on functional grounds despite a normal screen, professional and driving risk addressed formally, and the vascular drivers treated to target

optimal_actions.action: Disclose the diagnosis and its mechanism to the patient and the informant, and address driving, medication management, finances, advance care planning and caregiver support
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Patient and informant engaged in care planning; safety domains addressed

useless_tools.rationale: EEG has no diagnostic role in vascular cognitive impairment; it belongs to the differential of a rapidly progressive or fluctuating course (Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease, non-convulsive status, toxic-metabolic encephalopathy), none of which is present here

A presynaptic dopaminergic study answers the Lewy-body question, not the vascular one, and there is no spontaneous parkinsonism, no fluctuating cognition with hallucinations and no REM sleep behaviour disorder
Cardiac sympathetic imaging is a test for dementia with Lewy bodies and for autonomic failure; it says nothing about cerebrovascular disease

An untargeted paraneoplastic or autoimmune-encephalitis battery in a chronic stepwise decline with a hypertensive imaging burden is the archetypal expensive miss; the indication for those assays is a subacute multidomain syndrome
The MRI already obtained answers everything a CT could and more: CT cannot show microbleeds or cortical superficial siderosis, so it cannot grade the vascular burden this diagnosis rests on
There is no embolic lesion pattern to explain: the burden here is small-vessel, and a structural cardioembolic source would not account for it
Prolonged rhythm monitoring is for an unexplained embolic infarct pattern; in pure small-vessel disease it changes nothing about the diagnosis or the treatment

sequence_constraints.reason: Document the cognitive deficit before attributing it: imaging read without a cognitive profile invites over-attribution of incidental white matter change

critical_actions: Do not stop at a screening score in the normal range when an informant reports lost function
Obtain informant and employer accounts, and use a functional scale to establish severity
Estimate premorbid ability and interpret test scores against it rather than against population norms alone
Use ecologically valid executive tests where the screen is insensitive
Measure gait with a dual-task condition, which exposes the same executive failure objectively
Obtain MRI and relate the lesion distribution to the syndrome
Act on the professional and driving risk, which a normal screen had left unaddressed
contraindicated_actions: Do not reassure a patient with a normal screening score when instrumental and occupational function have been lost
Do not accept the patient's own minimising account as the functional history when insight is reduced
Do not allow continued unsupervised professional practice with fiduciary responsibility and a 1st-percentile planning score
Do not leave driving unaddressed after two reported near-misses with a documented dysexecutive syndrome
Do not attribute the errors to workload without formal testing
key_reasoning_points: The threshold between mild and major cognitive disorder is functional: independence lost, not a score crossed, and a screening instrument that misses this in a highly educated patient is a ceiling artefact rather than a negative result
Premorbid ability is the reference point — a MoCA of 26 with a premorbid IQ of 128 conceals a fall of more than three standard deviations on executive measures
Ecologically valid tests are the answer to a ceiling effect: the Multiple Errands Test and a planning task detected what the bedside screen could not
Dual-task gait testing gives an objective, quantitative marker of the same executive failure and does not depend on education
The risks in this case are external as well as personal: fiduciary professional responsibility and driving both require action that a normal screen had deferred

red_herrings.data_point: A MoCA of 26/30, within the normal range, with documented reassurance
red_herrings.intended_effect: Excludes dementia and closes the assessment, which is exactly what happened at the referring visit
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Screening instruments have a ceiling in highly educated patients; the diagnostic threshold is functional, and lost occupational function with 1st-percentile planning against a premorbid IQ of 128 meets it

red_herrings.data_point: The patient's own attribution of his errors to a heavy workload
red_herrings.intended_effect: Provides a benign explanation that the patient endorses and the clinician can accept
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Insight is reduced as part of the dysexecutive syndrome, which is precisely why the informant and employer accounts and the formal testing carry more weight than the patient's own

key_educational_points: Screening instruments have a ceiling: a normal score in a highly educated patient does not exclude dementia
The mild-versus-major threshold is functional, and an informant scale is the instrument that measures it
Ecologically valid executive tests detect what bedside screens miss
Dual-task gait testing gives an education-independent objective marker of executive failure
